title: Vitamin C facilitates direct cardiac reprogramming by inhibiting reactive oxygen species

predicted_errors.error_location: Methods, 'Generation of inducible cardiac reprogramming reporter in mouse embryonic fibroblasts' (MEF isolation)
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The text states 'α-MHC-GFP⁺ cells were sorted and cultured ... at a density of 10⁴/cm²' as the starting fibroblast population, yet the readout of the system is described later as 'After a successful cardiac reprogramming, GFP signal will become detectable in α-MHC-GFP MEFs'. Since αMHC-GFP marks cardiomyocyte-like (reprogrammed) cells, the starting fibroblasts must be GFP-negative; sorting and expanding GFP⁺ cells would make the reporter readout meaningless (the starting population would already be GFP⁺) and contradicts the quantification of GFP⁺% as reprogramming efficiency.

predicted_errors.error_location: Methods, MEF isolation ('In short, hearts were digested with 0.1% trypsin and plated on plastic dishes')
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The cells are called 'mouse embryonic fibroblasts (MEF)' obtained at embryonic day 13.5, but the described isolation digests hearts, which would yield (embryonic) cardiac cells/cardiac fibroblasts, not MEFs. Standard MEF isolation explicitly removes the heart and internal organs. The stated tissue source contradicts the cell type claimed and used throughout the paper.

predicted_errors.error_location: Methods, MEF GMT cell line generation
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: For MEFs only a single plasmid is listed ('MEFs were transfected with a PiggyBac vector carrying an inducible TetOn3G promotor, the mouse GMT reprogramming factors, and mCherry'), yet the next sentence refers to 'After co-transfection by using Lipofectamine 3000'. The PiggyBac system requires a transposase plasmid (as correctly described for the hFCF line, 'together with a transposase plasmid'); stable integration/puromycin selection as described cannot be achieved with the transposon vector alone.

The DEG criteria are stated as 'P-value < 10⁻⁶ and Log2 fold change ≥ 0.5 and ≤ (−0.5)'. As written this conjunction is impossible (no gene can have log2FC simultaneously ≥0.5 and ≤−0.5); the threshold should be |log2FC| ≥ 0.5 (i.e., ≥0.5 OR ≤−0.5). In addition, an uncorrected P < 10⁻⁶ cut-off with no mention of multiple-testing correction is inconsistent with standard DESeq2 reporting.

The reported evidence is that dehydroascorbic acid (lacking antioxidant activity) produced 'no difference in reprogramming efficiency'. A complete loss of effect would indicate that the enhancement is fully (not 'partly') dependent on the antioxidant property; conversely, the conclusion that the effect is only 'partially' mediated by ROS suppression is not supported by any experiment showing a residual, ROS-independent effect. The stated degree of dependence does not match the presented data.
